  How to Submit Public Comment

  In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit

  A. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 25-03, RELATED TO PERMANENT LOCAL
  HOUSING ALLOCATION (PHLA) YEAR 5 FUNDING AND PROPOSED
  ELIGIBLE ACTIVITIES

  The Los Angeles County Development Authority (LACDA), on behalf of Los
  Angeles County and its participating cities, will be applying for funding for Year
  5 of the Permanent Local Hosing Allocation (PLHA) Program from the California
  Department of Housing and Community Development. The allocation is based
  on real estate recording fees, and it is estimated that the City of San Gabriel will
  be allocated $135,222, from the $9 mission grant for the period July 1, 2025 –
  June 30, 2026 (Year 5). The City of San Gabriel has the opportunity to utilize this
  funding for the eligible housing activities as identified in the PLHA grant
  guidelines. If the State approves the eligible activities, the City is expected to
  expend the $135,222 reimbursable grant by June 30, 2028.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 18, 2025  3
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff Recommends that the City Council conduct a public hearing and adopt
  Resolution No. 25-03, which approves the following actions:

  1. Elect the following eligible activities, subject to the State approval, for Year
  5 of the 5-year PHLA grant period:

  a. The predevelopment, development, acquisition, rehabilitation, and
  preservation of multifamily, residential live-work, rental housing that
  is affordable to extremely low-, very low-, or moderate-income
  households, including necessary operating subsidies.

  2. Allocate, upon State approval, $135,222 of the Year 5 PLHA allocation
  toward eligible activity #1, and

  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute new contracts (and any other
  required documents) with LACDA for the 5-year PLHA Plan grant period and
  for Year 5 of the allocation and make adjustments as necessary to reflect
  the actual allocation of funds to San Gabriel.

  B. ORDINANCE NO. 718 AMENDING TITLE XI (BUSINESS REGULATIONS) TO
  ADD CHAPTER 127 OF THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO
  SIDEWALK VENDING AND AMENDING TITLE VII (TRAFFIC CODE) TO
  AMEND SECTION 72.012 RELATING TO PARKING BY PEDDLERS AND
  VENDORS (CA 25-001) – INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING

  In 2018 and 2022, the State passed Senate Bills 946 and 972, respectively,
  legalizing sidewalk vending with limited government regulations. Government
  Code Sections 51038 and 51039 prohibits cities and counties from adopting
  regulations that restrict the number of overall vendors from certain consents
  and approvals, and restrict the location for sidewalk vending. Cities may only
  adopt restrictions if such activities are found to include health, safety, or welfare
  concerns. The proposed Code Amendment (CA) would add Chapter 127 of the
  San Gabriel Municipal Code (SGMC) relating to sidewalk vending and amend
  SGMC Section 72.012 relating to parking by peddlers and vendors. The Fiscal
  Year 2024-2025 Adopted Budget includes the cost for required legal
  publication (Account No. 121-702-00-65-000) and codification (Account No.
  121-702-00-22-000) of the ordinance, if adopted by the City Council.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 18, 2025  4
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Conduct the public hearing and discuss proposed Ordinance No. 718;

  2. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 718 by title only:

  An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel, California,
  Amending Title XI (Business Regulations) to Add Chapter 127 of the
  San Gabriel Municipal Code Relating to Sidewalk Vending and
  Amending Title VII (Traffic Code) To Amend § 72.012 Relating to
  Parking by Peddlers and Vendors

  3. Waive future reading of the Ordinance and schedule the second reading
  and adoption of the Ordinance for the next regular City Council meeting.
  The Ordinance would then become effective 30 days after adoption.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. AWARD OF PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH HDL
  ECONSOLUTIONS FOR AN ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT THREE-YEAR
  ACTION PLAN IN THE AMOUNT OF $59,750

  The City of San Gabriel is dedicated to advancing its economic landscape and
  fostering sustainable growth through strategic planning. On July 15, 2024, staff
  released Request for Proposal (RFP) No. 24-04 for a three-year Economic
  Development Action Plan. The plan will serve as a roadmap to achieve key goals
  such as business retention, economic innovation, and sustainable growth. The
  contract amount is $59,750, to be funded and executed in two phases over two
  fiscal years. The Action Plan will guide the City’s economic growth strategies,
  including business expansion, retention, and attraction initiatives over the next
  three years.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 18, 2025  5
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute

  two annual phases- $29,750 for the current fiscal year and $30,000 for the next

MINUTES OF FEBRUARY 18, 2025
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Vice Mayor Menchaca called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order
  at 6:35 P.M. on Tuesday, February 18, 2025, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425
  South Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776, and announced that Mayor Wu was
  attending via teleconference from New Taipei City in Taiwan at the address listed on the
  Agenda.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Ding.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, Jorge Herrera Avila, Vice Mayor
  Denise Menchaca, and Mayor John Wu (via
  teleconference).

I  Council Members Absent:
  Staff Members Present:
  None.

  Rebecca Perez, Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Fire Chief

  Director Edward Macias, Acting Public Works Director

  5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 25-03, RELATED TO PERMANENT LOCAL
  HOUSING ALLOCATION (PHLA) VEAR 5 FUNDING AND PROPOSED ELIGIBLE
  ACTIVITIES

I  Vice Mayor Menchaca opened the public hearing.

  Acting Community Development Director Samantha Tewasart made the staff
  presentation.

  There was no public comment; therefore, Vice Mayor Menchaca closed the public
  hearing.
  Assistant City Attorney Koczanowicz clarified that item 3 of the staff
  recommendation should read, in relevant portion, "Authorize the City Manager to
  execute new contracts with LACDA (and any other required documents) .... "

  Discussion included the submission deadline.

  A motion was made by Council Member Ding, seconded by Council Member Chan,
  to adopt Resolution No. 25-03, which approves the following actions:

  1. Elect the following eligible activities, subject to the State approval, for Year S of
  the 5-year PHLA grant period:

I  a. The predevelopment, development, acquisition, rehabilitation, and
  preservation of multifamily, residential live-work, rental housing that is
  affordable to extremely low-, very low-, or moderate-income households,
  including necessary operating subsidies.

  2. Allocate, upon State approval, $135,222 of the Year S PLHA allocation toward
  eligible activity #1, and

  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute new contracts with LACDA (and any
  other required documents) for the 5-year PLHA Plan grant period and for Year
  S of the allocation and make adjustments as necessary to reflect the actual
  allocation of funds to San Gabriel.

  Motion carried by a roll call vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, HERRERA AVILA, MENCHACA, WU
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

I  B. ORDINANCE NO. 718 AMENDING TITLE XI (BUSINESS REGULATIONS) TO ADD
  CHAPTER 127 OF THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE RELATING TO
  SIDEWALK VENDING AND AMENDING TITLE VII (TRAFFIC CODE) TO AMEND
  SECTION 72.012 RELATING TO PARKING BY PEDDLERS AND VENDORS (CA
  25-001) - INTRODUCTION AND FIRST READING

  Vice Mayor Menchaca opened the public hearing.

  Acting Community Development Director Tewasart made the staff presentation.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 6  February 18, 2025
   Clarifying discussion included that associated fees will be presented for Council
  consideration in the Master Fee Schedule; provisions for trash disposal; kudos to
  staff for drafting the proposed ordinance; and that the state does not allow for
  refusal rights by adjacent business owners.

  There was no public comment; therefore, Vice Mayor Menchaca closed the public
  hearing.

  Discussion included the permitting process; enforcement and penalty provisions;

I  outreach to the community; ability to adjust regulations in the future in accordance
  with state law; addition of provisions for trash disposal; washing stations are
  covered by the public health code; the ordinance would affect uses in the public
  right-of-way; addition of a reporting feature on the City website; addition of tables
  and chairs verbiage to the ordinance; adding noise, lighting and signage provisions
  to the permit process; and reevaluation of an adopted ordinance at a future time.

  A motion was made by Council Member Chan, seconded by Council Member Ding,
  to:

  1. Waive full reading and introduce Ordinance No. 718 by title only: "An
  Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabriel, California, Amending
  Title XI (Business Regulations) to Add Chapter 127 of the San Gabriel Municipal
  Code Relating to Sidewalk Vending and Amending Title VII (Traffic Code) To
  Amend § 72.012 Relating to Parking by Peddlers and Vendors;" as amended to
  add language to Section 127.03 (H) regulating trash disposal, and adding
  Subsection (K) to regulating noise, lighting, and signage as part of the permit
  process.

I  2. Waive future reading of the Ordinance and schedule the second reading and
  adoption of the Ordinance for the next regular City Council meeting.

  Motion carried by a roll call vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, HERRERA AVILA, MENCHACA, WU
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS - None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. AWARD  OF  PROFESSIONAL  SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH  HDL
  ECONSOLUTIONS FOR AN ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT THREE-VEAR ACTION
  PLAN IN THE AMOUNT OF $59,750

  Acting Community Development Director Tewasart made the presentation,

I  clarified that the agreement would be with Hinderliter de Llamas & Associates
  (Hdl) rather than Hdl ECONSolutions, and introduced Hdl Principal/Managing
  Director Bill Foster.

  There was no public comment.

  Discussion included improvements to process to help move projects along;
  timeline for receiving reports; vacant and under-performing properties are part of
  the scope; and Hdl's experience with other cities.

  CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  Page 4 of 6  February 18, 2025
   A motion was made by Council Member Chan, seconded by Council Member
  Herrera Avila, to authorize the City Manager to execute a Professional Services
  Agreement with Hinderliter de Llamas & Associates in the amount of $59,750 to
  develop a three-year Economic Development Action Plan, funded in two annual
  phases- $29,750 for the current fiscal year and $30,000 for the next fiscal year.

  Motion carried by a roll call vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, HERRERA AVILA, MENCHACA, WU

I  NOES:
  ABSTAIN:
  ABSENT:
  NONE
  NONE
  NONE

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT - None.

  9. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  City Manager Lazzaretto reminded the community of the lanterns on display in Plaza
  Park and thanked Mayor Wu for arranging the display.

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Council Member Chan queried Mayor Wu about a lantern design element; and
  reported on his attendance at Alhambra's Lunar New Year Festival, a monthly Chinese
  American Citizens Alliance meeting, and a soft opening lunch at the San Gabriel
  location of Nern by Summer Rolls restaurant.

  Council Member Herrera Avila reported on a ride-along with Police Chief Elizalde.

I  Council Member Ding reported on his attendance at several Lunar New Year events
  including the San Marino Chinese Club Lunar New Year Festival, and meetings of the
  San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments (SGVCOG) Energy and Transportation
  Committees.

  Mayor Wu reported on his attendance at the opening ceremony of the Taiwan Lantern
  Festival in Taoyuan City, Taiwan, and his lantern selection for San Gabriel's next Lantern
  Festival, and thanked the Taiwan Tourism Administration for providing the lanterns;
  reported on the signing of a Sister City Memorandum of Understand (M.O.U.) with
  Magistrate Hsu of Hualien County; reported on a meeting with the directors and
  managers of Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office, and a meeting with Sister City
  Banqiao District Executive Director Chen Che-Cheng at which they planted a tree in
  front of the Banqiao District Office; and reported he would be meeting with the Taipei
  Youth Commission in Taipei City about a possible intern program. In closing, he
  thanked City Manager Lazzaretto for facilitating the Plaza Park lantern display.

  Vice Mayor Menchaca reminded all of the lantern display at Plaza Park until Sunday,
  February 23, 2025; announced the San Gabriel Police Department is accepting

I
  applications for their next Community Academy until March 5, 2025; reported on her
  attendance at a performance of the Amanda Castro Band at the Mission Playhouse;
  and encouraged all to check out future events on the Mission Playhouse calendar.

  11. CLOSED SESSION - None.
